english.title: Bring an animal onto Transport for London road transport premises after being refused access
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) brought an animal, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ANIMAL..),
onto a part of Transport for London road transport premises at **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..) to which it had been refused access
english.legislation: Contrary to byelaws 12(1) and 14 of the Transport for London Road Transport Premises Byelaws made under paragraph 26 of Schedule 11 to the Greater London Authority Act 1999 and confirmed under section 67 of the Transport Act 1962.

english.notes:
(i) See Byelaw 13 for the provision of a name and address by persons suspected of breaching this byelaw.
(ii) See byelaw 15 for a power to remove persons breaching this byelaw
(iii) See byelaw 16 for the requirement for authorised persons exercising any power conferred any of the Byelaws to produce a form of identification when requested to do so.
(iv) See Byelaw 17 in relation to the provision of notices.
(v) Byelaw 12(4) provides that if a person in charge of an animal breaches any of Byelaws 12(1) to 12(3), then that person:
(a) may be asked by an authorised person to remove that animal, and if he fails to do so immediately, then that animal may be removed by or under the direction of an authorised person;
(b) shall be liable to the Operator for the cost incurred by or on behalf of the Operator in removing and keeping it; and (c) shall be liable to the Operator for the cost of putting any property soiled or damaged back into its proper condition.
(vi) Byelaw 12(5) provides that a person in charge of an animal shall carry it when on a moving escalator on the premises, unless that animal is a trained assistance dog or police dog.
(vii) Byelaw 12(6) provides that any liability to the Operator under Byelaw 12(5) is in addition to any penalty for the breach of Byelaw 12.
